newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Corp says to buy 40,000 bpd Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Corp says to buy 40,000 bpd Iraqi oil.

text.p: Mitsubishi Corp said on Monday it had signed an agreement on Friday to buy 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi crude oil.

Industry sources say Mitsubishi is acting as an agent for five Japanese oil companies -- Japan Energy Corp (JOMO), Nippon Oil Co Ltd, Kashima Oil Co Ltd, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
A Mitsubishi spokeswoman said: "We have signed an agreement to purchase 40,000 bpd of crude oil with Iraq."

The deal is the first that has been signed between Iraq and a Japanese company under the U.N. oil-for-food deal, which allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of crude oil over six months to pay for food and medicine for its citizens suffering under sanctions.
She added that Mitsubishi had yet to submit the contract to the United Nations, which must approve all of the oil contracts with Iraq.
Shipping schedules to lift the crude have yet to be worked out among the five oil companies, industry sources close to the negotiations said.
They said that trying to coordinate the schedules of the five companies was proving to be difficult.
Since the start of the U.N. oil-for-food deal, U.N. overseers have approved five contracts, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.

U.S. firms Coastal Corp and Bay Oil began on Sunday to lift crude oil from the southern export outlet of Mina al-Bakr, Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said in remarks carried by the official Iraqi News Agency on Sunday.
It was the first crude oil to be loaded from the Gulf port since the U.N.-Iraqi deal was agreed to last week.
Other firms that have been granted U.N. approval include Turkish state oil company TUPRAS which has received permission to buy 75,000 bpd.
The loading of the first tanker for Iraqi oil at Turkey's Ceyhan terminal was nearly completed, Turkish pipeline officials said on Monday.
Private Italian oil refiner Oil Energy also said its contract to buy 10,000 bpd of crude over three months was one of the five approved by the United Nations.
France's Elf Aquitaine is also believed to have had its contract approved.
Mitsubishi will be lifting Basrah Light crude from the Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr, the company spokeswoman said.
Japanese oil refiners Cosmo Oil Co Ltd and Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd are also interested in making possible purchases of Iraqi crude oil.
Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp have already dispatched representatives to Baghdad for oil talks.
